intro: Professionals and everyday users convert cups (us) (cup) to pints (us) (pt) when working across us_customary and us_customary standards in culinary recipe scaling, beverage bottling, laboratory reagent preparation, and fluid tank capacity sizing. One cup (us customary) equals 0.5 pints (us), while 1 pint (us liquid) equals 2 cups (us). Whether you are verifying volume & liquid specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many pints (us) (pt) are in 1 cup (us customary) (cup)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.5 pints (us) (pt) in 1 cup (us customary) (cup), which rounds to 0.5 pt for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 pint (us liquid) equals 2 cups (us).

faqs.question: How do I convert cups (us) to pints (us) (cup to pt)?
faqs.answer: To convert cups (us) to pints (us), use the formula: pt = cup × 0.5. For example, converting 0.75 cup gives 0.375 pt.

faqs.question: What is 0.75 cups (us) in pints (us)?
faqs.answer: 0.75 cups (us) (cup) equals exactly 0.375 pints (us) (pt) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
